blockNote: Psycho Slider glide triggers (Bank 00): five trigger actor-defs (StairTriggerSouth/North/West/East/WestEntry; 29 actor-spawn records in scene_actors, one more through awB2_stair_climb, which JumpFar's to StairTriggerWestMain) plus the helpers LockPlayerForClimb, UnlockPlayerAfterClimb and RestorePlayerControl (the last is also called by three ramp exits in ramps.asm).
=== What a trigger detects ===

A trigger runs every frame in its own slot (D = trigger: $14/$16 = its pixel position, $0E = glide length). Y = the player actor. It fires only while Will is Psycho Sliding (RunAttackNS/RunAttackEW in player_character) through its tile: the player's animation index ($28) must be one of the two looping frames of ONE slide direction, and CheckMoveState requires the player's sprite bank ($7F0008) to be $8F, the will_alt spriteset that SetPlayerSpriteDirect #04 selects at the start of every slide.

Slide animation indices (will_alt spriteset): south $0C start / $0D loop / $0E finish, north $0F/$10/$11, west $12/$13/$14, east $15/$16/$17 (positive speed = south or east, negative = north or west). The old comments called these 'walk frames' and the bank check a 'walking state'; neither is true.

The trigger names do not match the slide direction they react to: StairTriggerSouth = WEST slide ($12/$13, glide X -4 per frame), StairTriggerNorth = EAST slide ($15/$16, X +4), StairTriggerWest = NORTH slide ($0F/$10, Y -4), StairTriggerEast = SOUTH slide ($0C/$0D, Y +4). The ClimbX routines move the player the same way the slide was already moving.
=== Geometry ===

Slide axis: exact pixel equality with the trigger (X for South/North, Y for West/East). Lateral axis: a 32-pixel window, trigger - 7 .. trigger + $18 inclusive (compare is trigger - 8 < player <= trigger - 8 + $20); the old '+/-$20' wording is wrong.
=== The glide ===

On a hit the trigger overwrites the player's entry pointer ($00/$02 of the player actor) with ClimbX and calls LockPlayerForClimb: $0E (the spawn record's type byte >> 1, InitActorFromSceneData mode 1) x 4 is stored as a frame countdown in the PLAYER's statsPtr ($7F0020), the player's velocity words are zeroed, D-pad input is masked (joypadMaskStd $0F00) and playerFlags $0800 is set. The player actor then runs ClimbX: once, $10 |= $2200 ($2000 = script-driven actor path, $0200 = slide-active flag that RunAttackFlagSetup also sets; its reader is unknown) and $10 bit $0008 (collision-aware movement) is cleared; then every frame the player's X or Y is changed by 4 px directly (no collision test) until the countdown reaches 0: 4 x $0E frames = 16 px per $0E unit (a $0E of 0 would run 65,536 frames). There is no animation during the glide; the slide's looping frame stays on screen.

Landing: clear $2000, stage the FINISH frame of the same slide ($14 west, $17 east, $11 north, $0E south), AnimOnce, then UnlockPlayerAfterClimb. That routine does what RunAttackCleanup does (clear $0200, consume the attack bit in joypadHeld, clear playerFlags $0002) plus clearing climbStateData ($09E0, in fact the ability damage bonus that attack_ability_system sets for the slide), re-enabling collision-aware movement and un-masking joypadMaskStd, then RestorePlayerControl returns the player to PlayerIdleEntry.

db-us/transforms.json (stair_climb) rewrites two vanilla constants: the attack-bit immediate (the vanilla ROM has a different bit, $0080 here after the button remap) and the joypadMaskStd consumption mask (ends in $FC here instead of the vanilla $F0). Comments here describe the post-transform values. Block is marked non-movable because of the tight $& coupling between triggers and climb handlers.

StairTriggerSouth: Glide trigger for a WEST-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $12/$13). Needs player X == trigger X exactly and player Y inside the 32-px window trigger Y - 7 .. trigger Y + $18, sprite bank $8F. On success the player is sent to ClimbSouth (X -4 per frame) and locked by LockPlayerForClimb. 1 spawn site.
StairTriggerNorth: Glide trigger for an EAST-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $15/$16). Needs player X == trigger X and player Y in the window trigger Y - 7 .. trigger Y + $18. On success the player is sent to ClimbNorth (X +4 per frame). 1 spawn site.
StairTriggerWestEntry: Entry variant of StairTriggerWest: shifts the trigger itself by (-8, 0) pixels once (NudgePosition on the trigger's own slot), then continues into StairTriggerWestMain. 1 spawn site.
StairTriggerWest: Glide trigger for a NORTH-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $0F/$10). Needs player Y == trigger Y exactly and player X in the window trigger X - 7 .. trigger X + $18. Starts with SetEntryHere so the check repeats every frame. On success the player is sent to ClimbWest (Y -4 per frame). 12 spawn sites (plus the awB2 JumpFar into StairTriggerWestMain).
StairTriggerEast: Glide trigger for a SOUTH-moving Psycho Slide (player animation $0C/$0D). Needs player Y == trigger Y exactly and player X in the window trigger X - 7 .. trigger X + $18. On success the player is sent to ClimbEast (Y +4 per frame). 14 spawn sites, the most used trigger.
CheckMoveState: Helper for the triggers: Y = player actor; carry clear when the player's sprite bank byte ($7F0008) is $8F, carry set otherwise. $8F is the bank of the will_alt spriteset (body_table entries 4 and 5), which the Psycho Slider selects with SetPlayerSpriteDirect #04; the normal Will spriteset is bank $95. It is not a 'move state' and the name is misleading.
ClimbSouth: Player-side glide for a west slide: entry flags once ($10 |= $2200, bit $0008 cleared), then X -4 per frame while the statsPtr countdown runs; at 0 it leaves script-driven mode, stages the west slide's finish frame $14 and calls UnlockPlayerAfterClimb.
ClimbNorth: Player-side glide for an east slide: X +4 per frame; finish frame $17.
ClimbWest: Player-side glide for a north slide: Y -4 per frame (up the screen); finish frame $11.
ClimbEast: Player-side glide for a south slide: Y +4 per frame (down the screen); finish frame $0E.
LockPlayerForClimb: Runs in the TRIGGER's context (D = trigger) right after a hit. Stores $0E x 4 (the glide length in frames; 4 px per frame, so 16 px per unit of $0E) in the PLAYER's statsPtr ($7F0020) as a countdown, zeroes the player's $2C/$2E/$08, masks the D-pad ($0F00 into joypadMaskStd) and sets playerFlags $0800 (script/ability lock). The countdown is left at 1 when the glide ends (the zero is never stored back).
UnlockPlayerAfterClimb: End of a glide, standing in for RunAttackCleanup (which the interrupted slide never reaches): zeroes climbStateData ($09E0, the ability damage bonus), clears the consumption bits from joypadMaskStd, sets $10 bit $0008 and clears $0200, consumes the attack press in joypadHeld, clears playerFlags $0002, then RestorePlayerControl.
RestorePlayerControl: Returns the player to normal locomotion: entry pointer = PlayerIdleEntry, $2C/$2E/$08 zeroed, $10 = ($10 and $FDFF) or $0008, D-pad un-masked ($0F00 from joypadMaskStd), playerFlags $0800 cleared. Called from UnlockPlayerAfterClimb and from three ramp exits in ramps.asm.

blockNote: COP handlers for the player's body spriteset and player-specific animation staging (Bank 00, 11 handlers, COP #8E-#98). The copdef names for #90-#92 are StagePlayerMoveX/Y/XY (the labels here are StagePlayerSpriteMoveX/Y/XY).

Script sites: SetPlayerSpriteDirect 24, StagePlayerSprite 93, StagePlayerSpriteMoveX 2, MoveY 21, MoveXY 9, RunPlayerAnim 8, StagePlayerSprFromDP 8 (all in forced_walk). StagePlayerSprWall and WallAnimHere/North/South have no script sites.
=== Body table ===

SetPlayerSpriteDirect takes an index into the 6-byte body_table entries (word spriteset pointer, bank byte, ...): 0 Will ($95), 1 Freedan ($8E), 2 and 3 Shadow ($94), 4 will_alt ($8F), 5 ability_fx ($8F), 6 freedan_fx ($97), 7 shadow_fx ($97), 8 shadow_mode ($97). It writes spritesetPtr ($7F0006), the bank byte ($7F0008), the table offset into animScratch2 ($7F000E, read by the sprite decomposer while playerFlags bit 15 is set) and the raw index into $0AC8, then sets playerFlags $8000. It does NOT stage an animation: no $28/$2A change. $7F0008 is polymorphic (sprite bank for sprite actors, amplitude for HDMA sine thinkers).
The StagePlayerSprite family calls SetActorBody instead, which picks the body from characterForm, so one script works for Will, Freedan and Shadow.
=== Staging ===

These ops store the raw animation operand in $28 (no ProcessAnimFlag, so no mirror handling), clear $2A, and save the next-op address in $00 and the script bank in $02 (the lines LDA $0C / STA $02 before each store are inserted by db-us/transforms.json and have no address tag). The movement operands of MoveX/MoveY/MoveXY are movement indices, not distances or durations: AnimFrameLookup turns each into the head of a delta chain (movement_delta_table) stored in $2C (X) or $2E (Y); moveXAlt/moveYAlt ($7F0018/$7F001A) keep the raw index. StagePlayerSprFromDP takes the animation index from the actor's $00 word, which the forced_walk helpers ReadDirSprite_* park there just before; the handler then overwrites $00 with the new entry address. RunPlayerAnim behaves exactly like AnimOnce (#89).
=== WallAnimHere/North/South (#96-#98, unused) ===

Take a joypad mask word and compare it with joypadCurrent for equality; on mismatch they continue without waiting. Only the Y alignment is checked (Y low nibble must be 0); when misaligned they animate without probing. The probe tile is at the actor (Here), Y - $10 (North) or Y + $10 (South). TileCollisionQuery already folds solid tiles and out-of-bounds into $000F, so the BIT #$00F0 test never fires and only the $000F compare detects a block (the actor flag $0004 is then set and the op continues). Otherwise, when the tile type equals playerWallType ($09B0) they run UpdateActorAnimation (yield while it runs, continue when it finishes); a different type continues without animating. $0018/$001C are the page-0 scratch pair read by TileCollisionQuery.

SetPlayerSpriteDirect: COP #8E with one byte operand (body_table index 0-8). Writes spritesetPtr ($7F0006) and the bank byte ($7F0008) from the 6-byte body_table entry, caches index x 6 in animScratch2 ($7F000E) and the raw index in $0AC8, and sets playerFlags $8000. Does not touch the animation index or frame counter. 24 sites (the Psycho Slider code uses #04 = will_alt).
StagePlayerSprite: COP #8F with one byte operand (animation index). Stores it raw in $28, clears $2A, applies the characterForm body with SetActorBody, then saves the next-op address in $00 and the bank in $02. 93 sites.
StagePlayerSpriteMoveX: COP #90 (copdef StagePlayerMoveX) with two byte operands: animation index and an X movement index. Same staging as StagePlayerSprite; the movement index is kept in moveXAlt ($7F0018) and AnimFrameLookup turns it into the X delta-chain head stored in $2C. 2 sites.
StagePlayerSpriteMoveY: COP #91 (copdef StagePlayerMoveY) with two byte operands: animation index and a Y movement index; the Y delta-chain head goes to $2E, the index to moveYAlt ($7F001A). 21 sites.
StagePlayerSpriteMoveXY: COP #92 (copdef StagePlayerMoveXY) with three byte operands: animation index, X movement index, Y movement index; delta-chain heads go to $2C and $2E. 9 sites.
RunPlayerAnim: COP #93 with no operands, identical to AnimOnce (#89): one UpdateActorAnimation pass; yields (PLA PLA RTL) while the animation runs, and on completion zeroes $2C/$2E and continues. 8 sites.
StagePlayerSprWall: COP #94 with four byte operands (animation index, X movement index, Y movement index, wall type). Same as StagePlayerSpriteMoveXY plus a fourth byte stored in playerWallType ($09B0) for the WallAnim ops. No script sites.
StagePlayerSprFromDP: COP #95 with no operands. The animation index is the low byte of the actor's $00 word, which the forced_walk helpers ReadDirSprite_XVelocity/YVelocity store there before the op; afterwards the handler overwrites $00 with the next-op address like StagePlayerSprite. 8 sites, all in forced_walk.
WallAnimHere: COP #96 with one word operand (joypad mask, compared for equality with joypadCurrent). If the masks differ the op continues at once. If Y is 16-aligned it probes the tile at the actor; a block (TileCollisionQuery returned $000F) sets actor flag $0004 and continues; a tile type different from playerWallType continues without animating; otherwise (or when Y is not aligned) it runs UpdateActorAnimation and yields until the animation finishes. No script sites.
WallAnimNorth: COP #97, same as WallAnimHere but the probe pixel is Y - $10. No script sites.
WallAnimSouth: COP #98, same as WallAnimHere but the probe pixel is Y + $10. No script sites.

blockNote: COP handlers that overwrite one metatile of LAYER 0 at run time (Bank 00, COP #4B-#4E) plus their helpers. Used by puzzle rooms, breakable walls and the item-use effects to swap floor/wall tiles.
Script sites: DrawMetatileAbs (#4B) 24, DrawMetatileHere (#4C) 8 (2 in pyD0_breakable_wall, 6 in item_use_system). WorldMapStream3 (#4D) and WorldMapStream4 (#4E) have no script sites.

All writes go to layer 0 only: collision flags come from $7F0000 + metatile ID (the layer-0 table; collisionFlagTableL1 sits at $7F0100 and is not used here), the map is $7EA000 + index (mapLayerTilemap), the collision map is $7FC000 + index, and the tile definitions are read from the hard-coded $7E2000 + ID x 8 (metatileDefBase is $2000 for layer 0, $2800 for layer 1). A tile is repainted on screen only when it lies in the visible window: horizontally (pixel X + 16 - bg1ScrollH) < $0111, vertically 0 <= pixel Y - ((mapScrollV - $10) and $FFF0) < $F1. Off-screen tiles only update the map and collision data.

The staged update is one 2x2 metatile: $0902 = VRAM word address of the top row (BG1 nametable at $1000 via PixelToVramAddress), $0908 = that + $20, tile words $0904/$0906 (top) and $090A/$090C (bottom). The NMI flush in event_blocks writes it and clears $0902; TileQueryGate makes the next draw wait until $0902 is zero again. The name tileQueryResult is a misnomer.

Direct page: the handlers run with D = actor; the stores to $0018/$001A/$001C/$001E/$0000 are absolute (page-0 scratch) and become the DP $18/$1A/$1C/$1E/$00 seen by ResolveTileData after TCD zeroes D. The page-0 $00 here is NOT the actor's entry word. DrawMetatileHere takes the actor's $14/$16 as TILE coordinates (no divide by 16); pyD0_breakable_wall converts its pixel position first and saves the originals in orbitAngle/orbitDiameter ($7F0010/$7F0012).

WorldMapStream3/4 stream one 3- or 4-byte record per call (X tile, Y tile, metatile ID, and for #4E a delay byte stored in the actor's $08 wait counter), cache the pointer in $24, rewind the script pointer by 2 and yield between tiles, and an X byte with bit 7 set ends the stream. extendedFlags ($7F002A) bit 1 = pointer cached, bit 2 = queue orbitAngle as a sound effect (sfxQueueCh2) per tile; nothing in the extracted scripts uses them.

DrawMetatileAbs: COP #4B with three byte operands: tile X, tile Y, metatile ID. Waits (rewinds the script pointer and yields) while TileQueryGate reports a pending update, otherwise converts the tile coordinates to pixels and calls ResolveTileData to update the layer-0 map and collision data and, when the tile is on screen, stage the 2x2 VRAM update. 24 sites.
DrawMetatileHere: COP #4C with one byte operand (metatile ID). Uses the actor's $14/$16 as TILE X/Y (the callers, pyD0_breakable_wall and item_use_system, must have converted pixel coordinates first), then behaves like DrawMetatileAbs. 8 sites.
WorldMapStream3: COP #4D with one word operand (stream pointer, cached in $24 on the first call). Each call paints one record (X, Y, tile ID) from the stream, optionally queues orbitAngle as a sound effect on channel 2 (extendedFlags bit 2), rewinds the script pointer by 2 and yields; a record whose X byte has bit 7 set ends the stream and the op continues past its 2-byte operand. No script sites.
WorldMapStream4: COP #4E, like WorldMapStream3 with 4-byte records: the fourth byte is stored in the actor's $08 (the wait counter), so it is a per-record delay, not a tile attribute. No script sites.
ParseMapEntry: Decodes the 3-byte record at stream address X: byte 0 = tile X (bit 7 set = end of stream, carry set), byte 1 = tile Y, byte 2 = metatile ID. Zero-extends (not sign-extends) the coordinates into DP $18/$1C, stores pixel positions (x16) in $1A/$1E and the metatile ID in $00, returns carry clear. Sets D = 0 itself.
ResolveTileData: Writes one metatile of layer 0: map index from TileCoordsToMapIndex (layer selector 0), collision byte from $7F0000 + ID copied to $7FC000 + index, the ID to mapLayerTilemap ($7EA000 + index). If the tile is inside the visible window it then copies the four tile words of the definition at $7E2000 + ID x 8 to $0904/$0906/$090A/$090C and stores the VRAM word addresses of the two tile rows in $0902 and $0908 (PixelToVramAddress, BG1 nametable). Off-screen tiles stop after the map writes.
TileQueryGate: Carry clear (proceed) when $0902 is zero, i.e. the previous 2x2 update has been flushed by the NMI. Otherwise rewinds the script pointer by 2 (back to the COP opcode, so the op runs again next time) and returns carry set; the callers then pop their return and yield.
